📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Twitch star Ibai Llanos left a small GTA 6 streamer in tears after encouraging his followers to tune into his broadcast, which had no viewers.

The launch of GTA 6 on November 19 saw countless content creators flock to Twitch to stream Rockstar’s long-awaited game, with some of the platform’s biggest personalities attracting enormous audiences.

However, Spanish streaming sensation Ibai Llanos decided to turn his attention to the other end of the spectrum, searching for a GTA 6 streamer with no viewers in the hopes of giving them a boost.

As reported by Meristation, Ibai discovered a Dominican streamer named Dicrim_RD69, who was broadcasting his playthrough of GTA 6 to an audience of zero people.

After joining the broadcast himself, Ibai left a simple “Hello” in the chat before encouraging his followers on social media to visit the channel, follow the streamer, and keep him tech giant.

His initiative worked, with Dicrim’s audience skyrocketing to 3,243 concurrent viewers within hours. Initially laughing in disbelief at his sudden popularity, Dicrim became overwhelmed with emotion after discovering Ibai was responsible.

“Thank you. You guys have brought me to tears,” he stated. “Ibai, I love you. I’ve been a fan of Ibai for a long time.”.

The pair subsequently spoke over a video call, during which Dicrim revealed that he had been streaming for more than a year without attracting much of an audience.

Recent findings suggest that “When you don’t have someone to talk to, to communicate with, you don’t feel the same. You feel bad,” he explained, admitting he had been feeling particularly upset the previous night.

Ibai reassured him by recalling his own beginnings as a content creator, revealing that he and his cousin used to stream basketball commentary to zero viewers when he was just 14 years old.

Industry observers note that “If it makes you happy, keep doing it,” Ibai encouraged him. Dicrim, who explained that his family couldn’t afford video games when he was younger, thanked Ibai for the gesture. “You made me the happiest man in the world,” he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An Indian YouTuber accused of stealing $1.8 million worth of jewelry has been forced to reenact the alleged heist for police after a distinctive tattoo helped investigators identify him.

On November 12, approximately 11.4kg of gold and diamond jewelry worth roughly 150,000,000 Indian rupees ($1.6 million) was discovered missing from a newly opened Tanishq jewelry showroom in Madurai, India.

Police believe the thief entered the building overnight using scaffolding at an adjacent construction site before descending through an unfinished elevator shaft and escaping with bags of valuables.

According to India Today, CCTV footage revealed that the suspect had visited the store three times before the robbery, apparently to familiarize himself with its layout.

Despite wearing a mask, a distinctive tattoo visible in the footage reportedly helped investigators identify him as 25-year-old YouTuber Nishanth Krishna.

Days later, Nishanth was arrested after a bus driver recognized him and alerted police. According to The Latest Indian Express, he allegedly attempted to escape through a bus window as officers approached.

#WATCH | Madurai, Tamil Nadu | Court grants one-day police custody of accused Nishanth in Tanishq jewellery showroom robbery case.The robbery took place on November 12 at the Tanishq jewellery showroom on the Madurai Bypass Road, where 11.384 kg of gold and diamond jewellery… pic.twitter.com/gGFBOcv9pb.

His girlfriend, fellow content creator Meenakshi Nachiyar and his father were also arrested in connection with the heist, with police alleging they helped conceal the stolen jewelry.

On November 20, Nishanth was taken back to the showroom and instructed to reenact the robbery, demonstrating how he entered the building, collected the jewelry, and escaped.

As reported by Hindustan Times, he was subsequently returned to Madurai Central Prison and remanded in judicial custody.

  • It has been revealed that after 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto fans have finally been able to sink their teeth into GTA 6 and all that Leonida has to offer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 boss Rob Nelson has explained why players aren’t able to play classic minigames like darts and bowling, despite there being some nods to them in-game.

It has been revealed that after 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto fans have finally been able to sink their teeth into GTA 6 and all that Leonida has to offer. Early on in the story, you’re introduced to one of the classic GTA mini-games: pool.

Industry observers note that however, if you look around The Rusty Anchor and other bars around the state of Leonida, you will notice that darts is missing. Plus, there is the Kingpin bowling alley in Port Gellhorn, but you can’t relive your days as Niko and Roman, tossing strikes down the lanes.

Well, Rockstar’s Rob Nelson told VGC that a “lot of work” is needed to get the minigames and activities right, but they “didn’t have the resources” to bring Darts and Bowling back.

“The darts one is a contentious one,” Nelson noted. “Even we… you hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to.”.

Nelson noted that gym activities, like Weightlifting, extend beyond just button mashing. “It mimics what weightlifting is,” he added.

Recent findings suggest that “A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right. Darts is one we just didn’t get to. It’s better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough.”.

The Rockstar North co-studio head added that pool has “proper physics” and is a “game in its own right.”.

Industry observers note that despite missing darts and bowling, Rockstar’s long-awaited release has paid off in spades. It has become the joint best-reviewed game of all time, matching Ocarina of Time.

If only there were a cheat code that could help you turn Jason into Luke Littler on a dartboard. That would have been a nice touch.

GTA 6 had been in development for a long time before it arrived on November 19. This means that many actors who appear in the game may have had to wait years to see their work fully realized in Vice City.

That’s exactly what happened to Guy A. Fortt, who is named in the GTA 6 credits. In fact, it’s been so long since he actually gave Rockstar his performance, he no longer remembers who he’s even playing.

Sources indicate that “So, I was a motion capture actor on GTA 6, but I don’t know who the hell I am,” Fortt explained in a video. “I auditioned about four or five years ago, they put the balls all over my body and face I was [gesturing], and then I forgot all about it.”.

“Then I get a random email telling me that I’m in GTA 6. This is where I need your help.”.

Industry observers note that “All I know is I was behind the counter, I was standing there. I know the leads came in, they were talking to me [and] I had balls and stuff all over my face, and I was talking to them about something,” he continued.

Industry observers note that based on this description, it sounds like he is some kind of store clerk. Perhaps he’s the owner of one of the many stores that Jason and Lucia can rob across Leonida.

The following day, he posted an update saying that three million players are currently on the hunt for his character, admitting he had “no clue” what Grand Theft Auto was or how massive it was.

Ex-Rockstar artist explains main difference between Red Dead 2 and GTA 6 open world

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (378 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A former Rockstar artist who worked on both GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2 says Leonida’s countryside has slightly less detail than the natural world of Rockstar’s Western.
  • Industry observers note that david O’Reilly made the comparison while exploring GTA 6’s Mount Kalaga region, an area he worked on before leaving Rockstar in 2023.
  • O’Reilly believes Red Dead 2 gave its landscapes more attention because they made up so much of the game’s world, while GTA 6 has a dense modern city to bring to life alongside its countryside.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A former Rockstar artist who worked on both GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2 says Leonida’s countryside has slightly less detail than the natural world of Rockstar’s Western.

Industry observers note that david O’Reilly made the comparison while exploring GTA 6’s Mount Kalaga region, an area he worked on before leaving Rockstar in 2023. He was impressed by what he found, describing the game’s presentation as “almost flawless,” but noticed a difference in where the two games put their detail.

O’Reilly believes Red Dead 2 gave its landscapes more attention because they made up so much of the game’s world, while GTA 6 has a dense modern city to bring to life alongside its countryside.

“I’m seeing a slight paring back in the natural world in GTA 6 from RDR2, but obviously a much greater emphasis and much more kind of detail in the urban environments,” O’Reilly said in a video sharing his first impressions.

He also found GTA 6’s cities more interactive and immersive, saying the difference reflected the kind of world each game was built to portray.

“GTA 6 is more a systems-driven modern urban world with countryside, natural landscapes, whereas RDR2 was almost purely natural landscapes,” he explained. This was especially noticeable in the game’s rivers, which he worked on as a water artist for Red Dead 2.

“Rivers were a bigger emphasis on RDR2. They were a significant part of the world, and in this game they’re a lesser part of the world,” he remarked. After examining the water around Mount Kalaga, O’Reilly added that, “on balance,” he prefers Red Dead 2’s rivers and thinks GTA 6’s water is generally “a little bit too slow.”.

He praised the way GTA 6’s water continues to react to players and objects even when they stop moving, though, calling it “a big plus point.” O’Reilly was also impressed by the riverbanks themselves, saying the rocks on either side were “blowing my mind.”.

Despite giving Red Dead 2 the edge when it comes to natural landscapes, O’Reilly expects to spend plenty more time travelling around Leonida. After a canoe trip through Mount Kalaga, he noted GTA 6 would probably replace Red Dead 2 as his “go-to chill game” when he wants to relax.

A woman who was praised as being a hero for fighting fires in Singapore has now been arrested for arson and is accused of starting those same fires.

If a fire hits, your first port of call should really be the emergency services so that they can dispatch some professionals. However, there are times when you have to fight the fire yourself, at least until the fire crew manages to get there.

Well, over in Singapore, 33-year-old Ong Siew Hoon took things into her own hands, fighting a set of fires that had been started in a trash chute in the building that she lives in.

According to recent reports, as a result, she was nominated for a community award that rewards such acts of bravery. However, as it turns out, the 33-year-old has been arrested on suspicion of starting the fires in the first place.

According to Asia One, Ong Siew Hoon was arrested on November 20 and was charged with one count of mischief by fire.

It has been revealed that as per reports, the 33-year-old was charged in court, with prosecutors asking for her to be remanded by police for a week while they carry out the investigation. Ong was also asked to help police revisit the scene and aid in the investigation as well.

She was also described as a “kind-hearted female resident” of the building, who remarked she had learned to use fire hoses in a bid to battle the constant flames in the building’s trash compartments and would check every hour for flames.

According to Mothership, if found guilty, the 33-year-old could face up to seven years in prison.

Ong was also expected to receive her community hero award on November 27, which is now the day she should be released from police custody.

A couple has been going viral after they were spotted arguing at a college football game, with television commentators narrating the whole thing.

If you go to a sports game, there is a chance that, at some point, you may end up on television or the jumbotron at the stadium. At that point, you don’t really want to be caught doing anything embarrassing, or you just might become a meme.

Well, on November 21, a couple attending the Wake Forest and Georgia Tech football game were caught in the middle of an argument towards the end of the game.

Now, there weren’t any mics attached to them, so you’d have to be a pretty good lip reader to figure out what exactly was said, but that didn’t stop the ESPN cameras from following along. “He wants an answer, and he’s not leaving. I mean, they are in each other’s personal space. He’s not happy with whatever she just told him,” ESPN announcer Jesse Palmer said.

Palmer’s co-commentator, Joe Tessitore, also weighed in with his own breakdown of what was going on, with the pair eventually urging the couple to settle things.

“This is kinda one of those moments where you just say, ‘I’m sorry. Please take a moment, and please say your goodbyes,'” Palmer concluded before the cameras turned their focus back to the on-field action.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as President and CEO after its Board of Directors unanimously voted to bring him back despite an ongoing investigation into national security concerns.

According to recent reports, huang had been temporarily replaced by Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress following reports that the executive had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The reports prompted the manufacturer’s board to establish an independent committee and retain outside legal counsel to investigate the matter.

On November 23, Nvidia announced that Huang would return to his leadership positions effective immediately following a series of meetings with the board and consultations with senior US government officials.

The controversy began in late October when The Latest York Times reported that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed whom US intelligence officials suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.

Megaspeed has also faced scrutiny over allegations that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia AI chips subject to US export restrictions. The Chinese government has denied the espionage allegations.

On November 8, Huang admitted in a message to Nvidia employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife. Nvidia announced its independent investigation that same day.

NVIDIA Board reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director.Read the release: https://t.co/x4bnjiSVil.

Further reporting alleged that Huang had also engaged in an extramarital affair with Nvidia Vice President of Healthcare Kimberly Powell. On November 12, the manufacturer revealed his resignation, ending his 33-year tenure as CEO.

However, less than two weeks later, Nvidia’s board reversed course, saying it was confident that Huang’s reinstatement posed no national security risk.

In a recent development, “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Board Chair Harvey C. Jones noted.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy controversy.

Nvidia releases independent investigation into CEO after reports of suspected Chinese spy link.

Nvidia CEO warns US of dangers surrounding Chinese chip war.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a latest industrial revolution,” Huang noted.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”.

Despite his return, Nvidia confirmed that its independent investigation remains ongoing and that Huang has committed to cooperating with it.

The tech giant has also established a National Security and Export Control Committee to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. Nvidia is additionally searching for a Chief Compliance Officer and will continue cooperating with government investigations.

“GTAVI-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. The hacker responsible for the massive GTA 6 leak in 2022 has been released from prison after receiving a seven-year sentence, with a judge warning him not to return to cybercrime.

Arion Kurtaj, 21, was sentenced at Woolwich Crown Court on November 23, but walked free the same day after already serving the majority of his sentence in custody.

According to the BBC, the former Lapsus$ hacker has been released on license and given a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order restricting his online activity, including banning him from using Telegram and Discord.

“You are a very talented young man,” Mr Justice Turner told Kurtaj before warning him: “Don’t let this happen again.”.

Kurtaj made headlines in September 2022 when he hacked Rockstar Games and leaked 90 clips containing nearly an hour of GTA 6 gameplay, revealing Vice City and the game’s two protagonists long before its official announcement.

Remarkably, the teenager carried out the attack while on bail for other cybercrimes, using an Amazon Fire Stick, a television, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse from a Travelodge hotel.

He also attempted to blackmail Rockstar, threatening to release the game’s source code unless the developer contacted him.

Rockstar later revealed that the breach cost the organization approximately $5 million to recover from, alongside thousands of hours of staff time.

In December 2023, Kurtaj was sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital after being deemed unfit to stand trial due to his autism.

At the time, the court heard that he remained highly motivated to commit further cybercrimes and could potentially hack Rockstar again.

However, a subsequent assessment found him fit to stand trial, and he was moved to a conventional prison in January 2026.

Even while behind bars, Kurtaj made headlines again in March after allegedly using a smuggled phone to post about GTA 6. He later pleaded guilty to possessing a mobile phone in prison.

On November 16, Kurtaj pleaded guilty to the Rockstar hack and several other cybercrimes involving companies including Uber, Revolut, and BT/EE.

His release comes just days after GTA 6 officially rolled out on November 19, more than four years after his original attack.

Meanwhile, Rockstar has faced another wave of GTA 6 leaks from the anonymous Cyberleek in 2026, including gameplay footage and claims of access to development builds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

TikTok star Ophelia Nichols, better known as Mama Tot, has spoken out after the man who fatally shot her teenage son was acquitted of murder.

Nichols, who has amassed over 12 million followers on TikTok, lost her 18-year-old son Randon Lee on June 24, 2022, after he was shot during an arranged drug deal outside a gas station in Prichard, Alabama, just one day before his 19th birthday.

On November 20, 2026, a jury found 25-year-old Reuben Gulley not guilty of murder following roughly 90 minutes of deliberations. Gulley had admitted to shooting Lee but maintained that he acted in self-defense.

In a post on Facebook following the verdict, Nichols described watching her husband break down in tears inside the courtroom.

“I have watched my husband break down sitting in that courtroom today while I did my best to hold it together for myself, for him, my children, our entire family,” Nichols wrote.

According to recent reports, “As I could feel the excited energy from the other side because their son was coming home, I slowly melted into my seat. Knowing that Justice had been stripped from my son and us, I couldn’t even describe what it did to my soul.”.

During the trial, Gulley testified that he had entered the back seat of Lee’s car to purchase two ounces of marijuana for $300. He claimed Lee pulled a gun on him after he took out the money, prompting him to open fire.

Prosecutors argued that Gulley shot the teenager to avoid paying for the drugs. Surveillance footage indicated him fleeing Lee’s vehicle with a gun in his hand, although it did not capture the shooting itself.

Following the acquittal, Nichols stated her family would continue to question how the jury reached its decision.

According to recent reports, “We don’t know what, why or how the jurors came to that decision and I’m sure we will question that moment the rest of our lives,” she wrote. “No remorse for our family. Zero regards for Randon’s life. What was done to our family was downright cruel and knowing that we are not alone in these situations is scary.”.

According to recent reports, “I watched my daughter cry her eyes out today, I’ve only seen my husband cry like three times in the 20 years we’ve been married and he couldn’t control himself today,” she noted. “He lost it.”.

An automated fire detection system at a ski resort in China has gone viral after repeatedly spraying water at a food booth’s sign, leaving viewers convinced it mistook pictures of flames for a real fire.

Footage of the bizarre incident demonstrates a ceiling-mounted water cannon blasting a barbecue stall’s flame-covered sign as confused onlookers watch.

The incident occurred on November 19 at Wanlong Ski Resort in Zhangjiakou, Hebei province.

As shown in footage, the automated system fires a powerful stream of water directly toward a sign decorated with images of burning charcoal.

The video quickly spread online, with viewers joking that the supposedly intelligent system couldn’t distinguish between a picture of fire and the real thing.

However, despite the apparent AI blunder, resort officials have offered a different explanation.

According to Yangtse Evening News, a visitor mentioned she had ordered lamb skewers shortly before the system activated, with water beginning to spray not long after cooking started.

Resort officials claimed the system was actually triggered by heat from a charcoal grill positioned behind the sign, rather than mistaking the flame graphics for a genuine blaze.

Recent findings suggest that staff rapidly shut down the equipment and cleaned the affected area, reopening it approximately 20 minutes later. No injuries were reported, and the resort has since adjusted the grill’s position to prevent another incident.

The footage comes amid growing scrutiny of automated detection systems and their mistakes.

In October 2025, a teenager was swarmed by armed police after an AI security system mistook a bag of Doritos for a gun.

More recently, a Pennsylvania high school was forced to scrap its AI security system after ordinary student belongings repeatedly triggered weapon alerts.

The competition took place on November 21 and was organized by FactMachine and Prez, drawing a crowd of spectators who were given the opportunity to vote for their favorite contestants.

The event was inspired by the ongoing controversy surrounding Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who had resigned as CEO just over a week before the competition took place.

Around 10 women participated in the competition, dressing up as spies and performing various espionage-inspired acts in front of the crowd.

Some contestants pretended to pull classified documents from their pockets, while another person dressed up as Jensen Huang joined in with the performances.

Spectators were able to decide the winner by scanning QR codes displayed at the venue and voting for their favorite participant, with a $50 cash prize up for grabs.

A post shared by Keri | NYC Content Creator (@keri_nyc).

The contest came after Nvidia launched an independent investigation on November 8 into reports that its CEO had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Huang also admitted to being unfaithful to his wife in a message sent to employees.

According to recent reports, on November 12, he resigned as president, CEO, and a member of Nvidia’s board of directors, ending his 33-year tenure leading the company. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO.

However, just two days after the lookalike contest, Nvidia announced that Huang had been reinstated following a unanimous vote by its board of directors.

Recent findings suggest that the company remarked it had consulted senior US government officials and was confident that his return posed no national security risk. Its independent investigation remains ongoing, with Huang committing to cooperate.

Discord’s new Auto Clips automatically saves gameplay moments when it hears a voice chat erupt in laughter or shouting, and it’s rolling out to Nitro members now.

Whether you’re playing a chaotic game of Fortnite or getting your friends together for another big Minecraft marathon, being able to instantly capture those moments that leave you in stitches of laughter is imperative.

After all, we’ve all been in situations where you’ve forgotten to hit record or your capture software has decided to stop working (it couldn’t be me). Enter Discord’s Auto Clips, a newly introduced feature that can detect when your group starts laughing or shouting before pulling together a clip of what just happened.

Unlike other capture software, Discord Auto Clips removes the need to hit a keyboard shortcut to record clips. Instead, it uses a small machine learning model that runs locally on the user’s PC, which continuously looks for audio cues resembling laughter or shouting, then uses those reactions to flag moments that might be worth saving.

Discord has revealed that the model cannot understand conversations or identify individual speakers, while any footage that is not saved as a clip is discarded after the gaming session ends.

Auto Clips can also work without voice chat in Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, League of Legends, and Rocket League. Discord uses integrations with those games to recognize events such as kills, goals, and completed rounds, with support for more titles planned in the future.

We've been cooking on Clips since Early Access released in 2023.Now there's 🢂Ａｕｔｏ Ｃｌｉｐｓ🢀When you and your friends break out laughing in voice, Discord saves the moment. No keybinds or additional setup needed. Starting today, Auto Clips is rolling out to Nitro… pic.twitter.com/a70itXDB1f.

Up to three highlights can be saved during each session, after which players can review them through Discord’s Clips library. It’s here that each recording can be trimmed, renamed, and edited with text or images, while game and voice audio can be removed before you share it with your friends or the wider internet.

Discord states clips remain stored locally on the player’s PC unless they choose to post them, and the company does not use saved footage, voice recordings, or other user data to train its detection model.

The feature began rolling out to Nitro members in Early Access on November 24 and is currently only available through Discord’s Windows desktop app.

AI breakthrough cuts energy use by 100x while boosting accuracy

📅 06 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (913 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence is consuming enormous amounts of electricity in the United States.
  • In a recent development, this rapid growth has raised concerns about sustainability.
  • The research comes from the laboratory of Matthias Scheutz, Karol Family Applied Technology Professor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial intelligence is consuming enormous amounts of electricity in the United States. According to the International Energy Agency, AI systems and data centers used about 415 terawatt hours of power in 2024. That accounts for more than 10% of the country's total electricity production, and demand is projected to double by 2030.

In a recent development, this rapid growth has raised concerns about sustainability. In response, researchers at a School of Engineering have created a proof-of-concept AI system designed to be far more efficient. Their approach could reduce energy use by up to 100 times while also improving performance on tasks.

A Hybrid Approach Called Neuro-Symbolic AI.

The research comes from the laboratory of Matthias Scheutz, Karol Family Applied Technology Professor. His team is developing neuro-symbolic AI, which combines traditional neural networks with symbolic reasoning. This method mirrors how people approach problems by breaking them into steps and categories.

The work will be presented at the International Conference of Robotics and Automation in Vienna in May and will appear in the conference proceedings.

Teaching Robots to See, Understand, and Act.

Unlike familiar large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and Gemini, the team focuses on AI systems used in robotics. These systems are known as visual-language-action (VLA) models. They extend LLM capabilities by incorporating vision and physical movement.

Industry observers note that VLA models take in visual data from cameras and instructions from language, then translate that information into real-world actions. For example, they can control a robot's wheels, arms, or fingers to complete a task.

Why Traditional AI Struggles With Simple Tasks.

Conventional VLA systems rely heavily on data and trial-and-error learning. If a robot is asked to stack blocks into a tower, it must first analyze the scene, identify each block, and determine how to place them correctly.

This process often leads to mistakes. Shadows may confuse the system about a block's shape, or the robot may place pieces incorrectly, causing the structure to collapse.

These errors are similar to the problems seen in LLMs. Just as robots can misplace blocks, chatbots can generate false or misleading outputs. Examples include fabricating legal cases or producing images with unrealistic details such as extra fingers.

How Symbolic Reasoning Improves Accuracy and Efficiency.

Sources indicate that symbolic reasoning offers a different strategy. Instead of relying only on patterns from data, it uses rules and abstract concepts such as shape and balance. This allows the system to plan more effectively and avoid unnecessary trial and error.

According to recent reports, "Like an LLM, VLA models act on statistical results from large training sets of similar scenarios, but that can lead to errors," said Scheutz. "A neuro-symbolic VLA can apply rules that limit the amount of trial and error during learning and get to a solution much faster. Not only does it complete the task much faster, but the time spent on training the system is significantly reduced.".

The researchers tested their system using the Tower of Hanoi puzzle, a classic problem that requires careful planning.

The neuro-symbolic VLA achieved a 95% success rate, compared with just 34% for standard systems. When given a more complex version of the puzzle that it had not encountered before, the hybrid system still succeeded 78% of the time. Traditional models failed every attempt.

Industry observers note that training time also dropped sharply. The new system learned the task in only 34 minutes, while conventional models required more than a day and a half.

Massive Energy Savings in Training and Use.

Sources indicate that energy consumption was reduced dramatically as well. Training the neuro-symbolic model required only 1% of the energy used by a standard VLA system. During operation, it used just 5% of the energy needed by conventional approaches.

Scheutz compared this inefficiency to everyday AI tools. "These systems are just trying to predict the next word or action in a sequence, but that can be imperfect, and they can come up with inaccurate results or hallucinations. Their energy expense is often disproportionate to the task. For example, when you search on Google, the AI summary at the top of the page consumes up to 100 times more energy than the generation of the website listings.".

The Growing Strain of AI on Power Infrastructure.

Sources indicate that as AI adoption accelerates across industries, demand for computing power continues to climb. Companies are building increasingly large data centers, some of which require hundreds of megawatts of electricity. That level of consumption can exceed the needs of entire small cities.

This trend has sparked a race to expand infrastructure, raising concerns about long-term energy limits.

According to recent reports, the researchers suggest that current approaches based on LLMs and VLAs may not be sustainable in the long run. While these systems are powerful, they consume large amounts of energy and can still produce unreliable results.

According to recent reports, in contrast, neuro-symbolic AI offers a different direction. By combining learning with structured reasoning, it may provide a more efficient and dependable foundation for future AI systems.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With GTA 6 bringing players back to Vice City, many are already thinking about how to get the most out of Rockstar’s next open-world game when it introduces.

With neon-lit streets, crowded nightlife, tropical beaches and surrounding landscapes of Leonida, GTA 6 is Rockstar’s most visually ambitious release yet.

While much of the conversation is focused on how consoles will handle it, the display you use is likely to make a more noticeable difference.

OLED technology has become increasingly popular thanks to its deep blacks, strong contrast, and vibrant colors. For a game featuring the diverse environments shown in GTA 6’s trailers, and especially paired with HDR, those advantages make upgrading your display the obvious choice.

Unlike traditional LCD monitors, OLED displays can turn individual pixels off completely, producing those luxuriously deep blacks. That will make GTA 6’s neon-lit streets, nighttime environments, and colorful landscapes look far more impressive.

For GTA 6, those improvements will be particularly noticeable in several environments players have already seen in Rockstar’s trailers:.

Modern OLED gaming monitors have also introduced technologies designed to improve brightness and visibility across different environments.

Industry observers note that GIGABYTE’s AORUS FO32U24G features a 32-inch 4K display built around a fourth-generation Tandem WOLED panel. Its RealBlack Glossy screen treatment is designed to preserve deep blacks and perceived contrast while reducing reflections.

Sources indicate that the monitor also features HyperNits, a technology that adjusts HDR brightness to help prevent images from appearing overly dark. According to GIGABYTE, HyperNits can increase overall brightness by up to 30% while preserving highlight details.

That will be particularly relevant to GTA 6’s varied environments, where players will frequently transition between bright sunlight, darker interiors, and nighttime scenes.

Although high-end gaming monitors are often associated with PC gaming, OLED’s picture quality advantages aren’t limited to players with expensive gaming computers.

GTA 6 is scheduled to launch on PS5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X|S.

Both the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S support modern display features, including HDR and up to 120Hz output in compatible games.

For console players, there are three main display features worth considering:.

GIGABYTE’s FO32U24G and FO27Q28G both feature HDMI 2.1 connectivity, making them options for players who use their monitors with consoles as well as PCs.

And while consoles won’t maximise these monitors’ refresh rates of 240Hz and 280Hz, OLED’s visual improvements will be just as glorious.

Even at lower frame rates, OLED’s contrast, black levels, and color reproduction will improve how supported games look. Of course, GTA 6’s final rendering resolution and performance modes remain dependent on Rockstar’s implementation.

Despite the advantages of OLED, burn-in remains one of the most common concerns surrounding the technology.

Burn-in occurs when uneven pixel wear leaves persistent image retention on a display. This can become a consideration when static elements remain visible for extended periods, including health bars, mini-maps, and other interface elements commonly found in video games.

For a game like GTA 6, where players could spend hundreds of hours exploring the open world, long-term display protection is worth considering.

Sources indicate that GIGABYTE addresses this with AI OLED Care Pro, available on the AORUS FO32U24G and FO27Q28G. The system automatically manages brightness, performs pixel cleaning during idle periods, and powers down the display when users step away.

It also includes Cooling Force technology, which uses integrated heat pipes to help manage panel temperatures during extended use.

While OLED technology offers several advantages, choosing the right display involves more than simply deciding between OLED and LCD.

Screen size, resolution, panel technology, and room lighting can all influence which monitor makes the most sense.

For players prioritizing GTA 6’s visual presentation, GIGABYTE’s FO32U24G offers a 32-inch 4K Tandem WOLED panel, while the FO27Q28G provides a smaller 27-inch QHD alternative with a 280Hz refresh rate.

GIGABYTE’s M series also includes several options for players with different preferences:.

Recent findings suggest that the MO27Q28G and MO27Q28GR are particularly relevant for players deciding between matte-style anti-reflection and glossy OLED displays. Both feature fourth-generation Tandem WOLED panels, but their different screen treatments may appeal to different gaming environments.

Meanwhile, the MO27Q2A provides an alternative OLED panel technology, featuring QD-OLED panel with 1.5M:1 contrast ratio for deeper black and richer details.

Ultimately, choosing a monitor for GTA 6 depends on the display someone already owns and what they want to improve, but OLED’s contrast, black levels, and color reproduction will provide a noticeable visual upgrade.

#92966. This newly introduced chip survives 1300°F (700°C) and could change AI forever

This newly introduced chip survives 1300°F (700°C) and could change AI forever

📅 07 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1255 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Modern electronics power everything from smartphones to satellites, but they all share a major limitation.
  • Researchers at the University of Southern California now believe they have found a way past that limit.
  • In a study published on March 26, 2026 in Science, a team led by Joshua Yang, Arthur B.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Modern electronics power everything from smartphones to satellites, but they all share a major limitation. Heat. Once temperatures climb above roughly 200 degrees Celsius, most devices begin to break down. For decades, this thermal barrier has been one of the toughest challenges in engineering.

Researchers at the University of Southern California now believe they have found a way past that limit.

In a study published on March 26, 2026 in Science, a team led by Joshua Yang, Arthur B. Freeman Chair Professor at the Ming Hsieh Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the USC Viterbi School of Engineering and the USC School of Advanced Computing, unveiled a upcoming type of memory device that continues to operate at 700 degrees Celsius (~1300 degrees Fahrenheit). That temperature exceeds molten lava and goes far beyond anything previously achieved for this class of technology. The device showed no sign of failure. In fact, 700 degrees was simply the maximum their equipment could test.

Industry observers note that "You may call it a revolution," Yang stated. "It is the best high-temperature memory ever demonstrated.".

A Memristor Built for Extreme Heat.

Industry observers note that the latest device is known as a memristor, a nanoscale component that can both store data and perform computations. It is constructed like a microscopic layered structure, with two electrodes on either side and a thin ceramic layer in between.

Jian Zhao, the study's first author, built the device using tungsten for the top electrode, hafnium oxide ceramic in the middle, and graphene for the bottom layer. Tungsten has the highest melting point of any element, while graphene, a single-atom-thick sheet of carbon, is known for its exceptional strength and heat resistance.

In a recent development, this combination produced remarkable performance. The device retained data for more than 50 hours at 700 degrees without needing to be refreshed. It also endured over one billion switching cycles at that temperature and operated at just 1.5 volts with speeds measured in tens of nanoseconds.

It has been revealed that the discovery was not part of the team's original plan. They were initially attempting to create a different graphene-based device, which did not work as intended. Along the way, they encountered something surprising.

According to recent reports, "To be honest, it was by accident, as most discoveries are," Yang said. "If you can predict it, it's usually not surprising, and probably not significant enough.".

Industry observers note that further investigation revealed why the device performed so well. In conventional electronics, heat causes metal atoms in the top electrode to slowly migrate through the ceramic layer. Eventually, they reach the bottom electrode, creating a permanent connection that short-circuits the device and leaves it stuck in the on state.

Recent findings suggest that graphene prevents this failure. Its interaction with tungsten is, as Yang described it, similar to oil and water. Tungsten atoms that approach the graphene surface cannot attach to it. Without a stable point to settle, they drift away instead of forming a conductive bridge. This prevents short circuits and preserves the device's function even under extreme heat.

The researchers confirmed this mechanism using advanced electron microscopy, spectroscopy, and quantum-level simulations. By understanding what happens at the atomic interface, they have turned an unexpected result into a principle that could guide future designs. Other materials with similar surface properties could be identified, which may help scale the technology for industrial production.

Applications in Extreme Environments.

In a recent development, electronics capable of operating above 500 degrees Celsius have long been a goal for space exploration. Venus, for example, has a surface temperature around that level, and every lander sent there has failed in part due to extreme heat. Current silicon-based chips cannot survive such conditions.

"We are now above 700 degrees, and we suspect it will go higher," Yang noted.

The potential applications go far beyond space missions. Geothermal energy systems require electronics that can function deep underground, where surrounding rock can glow red-hot. Nuclear and fusion systems also expose equipment to intense heat. Even in everyday settings, durability improves significantly. A device rated for 700 degrees would be extremely robust at the roughly 125-degree temperatures often reached inside automotive electronics.

Why It Matters for Artificial Intelligence.

Industry observers note that in addition to storing data, the device offers a major advantage for artificial intelligence. Many AI systems rely heavily on matrix multiplication, a mathematical operation used in tasks like image recognition and language processing. Traditional computers perform these calculations step by step, consuming large amounts of energy.

Memristors approach the problem differently. By using Ohm's Law, where voltage times conductance equals current, the device performs calculations directly as electricity flows through it. The result is obtained instantly as the measured current.

"Over 92 percent of the computing in AI systems like ChatGPT is nothing but matrix multiplication," Yang stated. "This type of device can perform that in the most efficient way, orders of magnitude faster and at lower energy.".

Yang and three co-authors of the study (Qiangfei Xia, Miao Hu, and Ning Ge) have already co-founded a company called TetraMem to commercialize memristor-based AI chips at room temperature. Their lab is already using working chips from TetraMem for machine learning tasks. The high-temperature version described in this research could extend those capabilities to environments where traditional electronics cannot operate, allowing devices such as spacecraft or industrial sensors to process data directly on site.

From Lab Prototype to Real-World Technology.

Despite the promising results, Yang emphasizes that practical applications are still some distance away. Memory is only one part of a complete computing system. High-temperature logic circuits will also need to be developed and integrated. In addition, the current devices were built manually at very small scales in a laboratory setting, so manufacturing at scale will take time.

"This is the first step," Yang remarked. "It's still a long way to go. But logically, you can see: now it makes it possible. The missing component has been made.".

In a recent development, from a manufacturing perspective, two of the materials used in the device, tungsten and hafnium oxide, are already widely used in semiconductor production. Graphene is newer but is actively being developed by major companies such as TSMC and Samsung, and it has already been produced at wafer scale in research environments.

Industry observers note that the work was conducted through the CONCRETE Center, short for Center of Neuromorphic Computing under Extreme Environments, a multi-university Center of Excellence led by USC and supported by the Air Force Office of Scientific Research and the Air Force Research Laboratory. Key experimental work was carried out in collaboration with Dr. Sabyasachi Ganguli's team at the AFRL Materials Lab in Dayton, Ohio, while theoretical analysis involved USC researchers and collaborators at Kumamoto University in Japan.

For Yang, publication in Science reflects more than a single achievement.

In a recent development, "Space exploration has never been so real, so close, and at such a large scale," he noted. "This paper represents a critical leap into a much larger, more exciting frontier.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As data centers consume more energy to support growing digital demands, engineers at the University of California San Diego have introduced a latest chip design that could make powering graphics processing units (GPUs) more efficient.
  • The findings, published in Nature Communications, suggest the potential for smaller and more energy-efficient systems in advanced computing environments.
  • Rethinking DC-DC Converters for Modern Electronics.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As data centers consume more energy to support growing digital demands, engineers at the University of California San Diego have introduced a latest chip design that could make powering graphics processing units (GPUs) more efficient. The innovation focuses on a key function in electronics: converting high voltages into the lower levels required by computing hardware. In laboratory testing, a prototype chip successfully performed this type of voltage conversion with high efficiency under conditions similar to those found in modern data centers.

The findings, published in Nature Communications, suggest the potential for smaller and more energy-efficient systems in advanced computing environments.

Rethinking DC-DC Converters for Modern Electronics.

At the center of the latest design is an improved version of a widely used component known as a DC-DC step-down converter. These converters are found in nearly all electronic devices and serve as a critical link between power sources and sensitive circuits. Their job is to take a high incoming voltage and reduce it to the exact level needed for safe operation.

In data centers, electricity is often distributed at 48 volts, while GPU processors typically require much lower voltages, usually between 1 and 5 volts. Efficiently managing this large voltage drop has become increasingly challenging as computing systems grow more powerful and compact.

Limits of Traditional Power Conversion Technology.

In a recent development, conventional step-down converters often struggle when dealing with large differences between input and output voltage. As that gap increases, efficiency drops and it becomes harder to supply enough current. Most existing designs rely on magnetic components such as inductors. While these components have been refined over many years, they are approaching their practical limits and are becoming harder to improve further.

"We've gotten so good at designing inductive converters that there's not really much room left to improve them to meet future needs," stated study senior author Patrick Mercier, professor in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering.

Exploring Piezoelectric Resonators as an Alternative.

To move beyond these limitations, Mercier and his team, including first author Jae-Young Ko, an electrical and computer engineering Ph.D. student at UC San Diego, investigated a different approach using piezoelectric resonators. These small devices store and transfer energy through mechanical vibrations rather than magnetic fields.

According to recent reports, converters based on piezoelectric components could offer several advantages. They have the potential to be smaller, more energy dense, more efficient, and easier to manufacture at scale. "They have a lot of room to grow and have the potential to deliver better performance than anything that's come before them," Mercier remarked.

However, earlier versions of piezoelectric converters have had difficulty maintaining efficiency and delivering sufficient power when handling large voltage differences.

Hybrid Design Achieves High Efficiency and Power Output.

To overcome these concerns, the researchers created a hybrid converter that combines a piezoelectric resonator with small, commercially available capacitors arranged in a carefully designed configuration. This setup enables the system to handle larger voltage conversions more effectively.

Industry observers note that the team incorporated this design into a prototype chip and tested its performance. The device successfully converted 48 volts down to 4.8 volts -- a level commonly required in data centers -- with a peak efficiency of 96.2 percent. It also delivered roughly four times more output current than previous piezoelectric-based designs.

It has been revealed that this hybrid approach offers several benefits. It creates multiple pathways for energy to move through the system, reduces wasted power, and lessens the strain on the resonator. Together, these improvements enhance both efficiency and power delivery while only slightly increasing the chip's size.

Challenges and Next Steps for Real-World Use.

Sources indicate that although the technology demonstrates strong promise, it is still in the early stages of development. The researchers view it as an notable step toward overcoming the constraints of current power conversion systems. Future efforts will focus on refining materials, improving circuit designs, and developing better packaging methods.

One challenge is that piezoelectric resonators physically vibrate, which means they cannot be attached to circuit boards using standard soldering techniques. New integration strategies will be needed to incorporate them into electronic systems, Mercier explained.

"Piezoelectric-based converters aren't quite ready to replace existing power converter technologies yet," Mercier added. "But they offer a trajectory for improvement. We need to continue to improve on multiple areas -- materials, circuits and packaging -- to make this technology ready for data center applications.".

This project was supported in part by the Power Management Integration Center (PMIC), an Industry-University Cooperative Research Center (IUCRC) funded by the National Science Foundation (award number 2052809).

#92962. Industry News: “Giant superatoms” could finally solve quantum computing’s biggest problem

📅 13 Apr 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1122 w)

Industry News: “Giant superatoms” could finally solve quantum computing’s biggest problem

📅 13 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1122 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden have introduced a upcoming theoretical design for quantum systems based on what they call "giant superatoms." This concept offers a fresh way to protect, control, and share quantum information, potentially bringing scientists closer to building large-scale quantum computers.
  • Quantum computers are expected to transform fields like drug discovery and encryption by solving problems that are far beyond the reach of conventional machines.
  • Recent findings suggest that "Quantum systems are extraordinarily powerful but also extremely fragile.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden have introduced a upcoming theoretical design for quantum systems based on what they call "giant superatoms." This concept offers a fresh way to protect, control, and share quantum information, potentially bringing scientists closer to building large-scale quantum computers.

Quantum computers are expected to transform fields like drug discovery and encryption by solving problems that are far beyond the reach of conventional machines. However, progress has been limited by a major challenge known as decoherence. This occurs when quantum bits, or qubits, lose their information due to interactions with their surroundings. Even small amounts of electromagnetic noise can disrupt the fragile quantum states needed for computation.

Recent findings suggest that "Quantum systems are extraordinarily powerful but also extremely fragile. The key to making them useful is learning how to control their interaction with the surrounding environment," says Lei Du, postdoctoral researcher in applied quantum technology at Chalmers.

According to recent reports, lei Du is the lead author of a study that outlines this new type of quantum system. The design is built around giant superatoms, which combine several important features. These systems reduce decoherence, remain stable, and consist of multiple interconnected "atoms" that function together as a single unit.

According to recent reports, giant superatoms bring together two previously separate ideas in quantum physics: giant atoms and superatoms. While each has been studied on its own, this is the first time they have been merged into a single system. These structures behave like atoms but are not found in nature. Instead, they are engineered by scientists (see fact box below).

Giant Atoms and Their "Quantum Echo".

The idea of giant atoms was first introduced by researchers at Chalmers over a decade ago and is now widely used in the field. A giant atom is typically designed as a qubit (which is the smallest unit of quantum information). Unlike ordinary atoms, it connects to light or sound waves at multiple, physically separated points. This allows it to interact with its environment in several places at once, helping it preserve quantum information.

"Waves that leave one connection point can travel through the environment and return to affect the atom at another point -- similar to hearing an echo of your own voice before you've finished speaking. This self-interaction leads to highly beneficial quantum effects, reduces decoherence and gives the system a form of memory of past interactions," explains Anton Frisk Kockum, Associate Professor of Applied Quantum Physics at Chalmers and co-author of the study.

Extending Entanglement Across Distances.

In a recent development, although giant atoms have improved understanding of quantum behavior, they have had limitations when it comes to entanglement. Entanglement allows multiple qubits to share a single quantum state and act as one coordinated system, which is essential for powerful quantum computers.

Recent findings suggest that to overcome this limitation, the research team combined giant atoms with the concept of superatoms. A superatom consists of several natural atoms that share the same quantum state and behave collectively as one larger atom.

This combination is expected to make it easier to create complex quantum states needed for quantum communication, networks, and highly sensitive measurement systems.

Recent findings suggest that "A giant superatom may be envisaged as multiple giant atoms working together as a single entity, exhibiting a non-local interaction between light and matter. This enables quantum information from multiple qubits to be stored and controlled within one unit, without the need for increasingly complex surrounding circuitry," explains Lei Du.

"Giant superatoms open the door to entirely new capabilities, giving us a powerful new toolbox. They allow us to control quantum information and create entanglement in ways that were previously extremely difficult, or even impossible," says Janine Splettstoesser, Professor of Applied Quantum Physics at Chalmers and co-author of the study.

Toward Scalable and Practical Quantum Systems.

Industry observers note that this work creates fresh possibilities for building quantum systems that are both scalable and reliable. The researchers strategy to move from theory toward actually constructing these systems. Their design could also be integrated with other quantum technologies, serving as a building block for connecting different types of quantum platforms.

Sources indicate that "There is currently strong interest in hybrid approaches, in which different quantum systems work together, because each has its own strengths," says Anton Frisk Kockum. "Our research shows that smart design can reduce the need for increasingly complex hardware and giant superatoms are bringing us one step closer to practically applicable quantum technology.".

Controlling Quantum Information Flow.

More on: Methods for protecting, controlling and distributing quantum information.

The study reveals that the way giant superatoms interact with light depends on their internal quantum states. This discovery gives researchers greater control over how quantum information moves through a system. They describe two different ways of connecting these structures to achieve useful outcomes.

It has been revealed that in one setup, several giant superatoms are closely linked in a specific arrangement. This allows them to pass quantum states between each other without decoherence, meaning no information is lost.

In another setup, the atoms are spaced farther apart but connected in a carefully tuned way so that waves remain synchronized. This makes it possible to direct quantum signals and distribute entanglement over long distances.

Understanding Giant Atoms and Superatoms.

Superatoms and giant atoms are engineered systems that behave like atoms rather than naturally occurring ones.

A superatom is a quantum system made up of multiple natural atoms that share a single quantum state and respond to light as one entity.

A giant atom, on the other hand, connects to light or sound waves at several separate points in space. It is called "giant" because it is larger than the wavelength of the light it interacts with.

Sources indicate that giant atoms have defined energy levels and follow the rules of quantum mechanics, yet they can reach sizes of up to millimeters, making them visible to the naked eye. Through electromagnetic or acoustic waves, they can interact with their surroundings at multiple locations at the same time. One way to picture this is as a single atom linked to a wave at several distant points. This unusual setup allows the atom to be influenced by the waves it produces.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that western intelligence agencies believe that Russia could be readying the launch of a nuclear-armed satellite before the end of the year. The satellite, called Sputnik-S, is believed to have been in development for the last several years, with the United States first warning of Russia's plans in February 2023. Now, a German news report believes that the country's armed forces are already "raising the alarm" about the potential impact such a satellite could have. According to one expert, such a weapon could knock out a third of low Earth orbit satellites instantly, eventually disabling all of them with a devastating impact on the planet as a whole. With satellites playing such a vital role for civilian life as well as both military and intelligence operations, it's easy to see why Russia may want such satellite-crippling capabilities.

The report notes that information about Sputnik-S has been exchanged between several NATO member countries, with intelligence agencies having already warned that a launch could happen within 60 days. That report was made in early November, suggesting that Sputnik-S could be in orbit and operational in early December. The Russian embassy in Germany rejected the "unfounded allegations," saying that they are nothing more than "part of a propaganda campaign" against the country.

Perhaps worryingly, the United States Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) published its own report in which it warned that "Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon." Such a move would be a violation of the 1967 Outer Space Treaty. The treaty prohibits any country from launching anything carrying nuclear weapons or, indeed, any weapon of mass destruction into Earth orbit. While there has been no suggestion that Russia could turn the nuclear weapons towards the planet, Sputnik-S would still clearly be in breach of the longstanding treaty. One expert cited by the report says that a nuclear explosion in space would knock out one-third of low Earth orbit satellites instantly, with the remaining satellites gradually failing in the following months. The EMP generated could even cause widespread technical carnage on Earth.

It has been revealed that as for which satellites could be a potential target for Sputnik-S, there is no shortage of options. SpaceX Starlink satellites are relied upon around the globe for their ability to provide fast, reliable networking to parts of the world not served by traditional connectivity options. Notably, Starlink has been used by Ukraine as it defends itself amid Russian aggression. But amid SpaceX's limiting of performance, Ukrainian officials have chosen to use their own "flying modems" to avoid relying on Elon Musk's tech giant. Russia has been trying to launch its own Starlink rival, with limited success. September saw it lose a batch of 16 satellites during launch.

Tech Report: This simple change stops robot swarms from getting stuck

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that imagine a swarm of robots rushing to complete an urgent job, such as cleaning up an oil spill or assembling complex machinery.
  • Industry observers note that this raises a simple but important question: in a limited area, how many robots can you deploy before efficiency starts to drop?
  • Sources indicate that A fresh study from the lab of L.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that imagine a swarm of robots rushing to complete an urgent job, such as cleaning up an oil spill or assembling complex machinery. At first, adding more robots speeds things up. But after a certain point, the space becomes crowded, robots start interfering with one another, and overall progress slows.

Industry observers note that this raises a simple but important question: in a limited area, how many robots can you deploy before efficiency starts to drop? Researchers at Harvard believe they have found a clear answer.

A Simple Idea That Boosts Efficiency.

Sources indicate that A fresh study from the lab of L. Mahadevan, the Lola England de Valpine Professor of Applied Mathematics, Organismic and Evolutionary Biology, and Physics, shows that adding a controlled amount of randomness to how robots move can reduce congestion and improve performance in crowded environments.

The work combines mathematical modeling, computer simulations, and real-world experiments. It demonstrates how basic local movement rules can lead to organized, efficient outcomes on a larger scale. The findings could influence how robotic fleets are designed and may even apply to human crowd management and traffic flow. The research was published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences and led by applied mathematics Ph.D. student Lucy Liu, with guidance from SEAS Senior Research Fellow Justin Werfel.

Why Randomness Helps Predict Complex Behavior.

Studying dense crowds is difficult because individuals can take countless possible paths and interact in unpredictable ways, Liu explained. To simplify the problem, the researchers treated each robot as a basic unit with a small, adjustable amount of variation in its movement.

"This might be counterintuitive, because how could randomness make things easier to work with?" noted Liu. "But in this case, when you have a lot of randomness, it becomes possible to take averages -- average distances, average times, average behaviors. This makes it a lot easier to make predictions.".

Simulating Robot Swarms in Motion.

To explore this idea, the team created computer simulations of robot groups, referred to as agents. Each agent started at a random location and was assigned a random destination. Once it reached its target, it immediately received a new one, mimicking continuous task assignment in real-world systems.

Recent findings suggest that each agent moved toward its goal with a tunable amount of variation, described as "noise." With no noise, agents moved in straight lines. With high noise, their paths became erratic and inefficient. However, this wandering also helped them navigate around one another.

Finding the "Goldilocks Zone" of Noise.

Industry observers note that the simulations revealed a clear pattern. When agents moved in perfectly straight paths, they rapidly formed dense clusters and traffic jams that halted progress. When movement became too random, congestion disappeared but efficiency dropped due to excessive wandering.

It has been revealed that between these extremes, the researchers identified a sweet spot. In this range, agents occasionally bumped into one another and formed short-lived clusters, but still managed to slip past and keep moving. This balance allowed the system to maintain a steady flow.

From Simulations to Mathematical Models.

Using these insights, the team developed formulas to estimate "goal attainment rate," or how many destinations are reached over time. These equations made it possible to determine the ideal combination of crowd density and movement randomness to maximize performance.

Testing the Theory With Real Robots.

According to recent reports, to confirm their findings, Liu collaborated with physicist Federico Toschi at Eindhoven University of Technology in the Netherlands. Together, they set up experiments with small wheeled robots in a lab equipped with an overhead camera.

Each robot carried a QR code so its position could be tracked and updated with fresh destinations. Although the physical robots moved more slowly and less precisely than the simulated agents, they displayed the same overall patterns.

The experiments supported a key idea: highly complex coordination does not require advanced intelligence or centralized control. Instead, simple local rules can produce effective group behavior, at least within certain density limits.

Industry observers note that "Understanding how active matter, whether it is a swarm of ants, a herd of animals, or a group of robots, become functional and execute tasks in crowded environments using the principles of self-organization, is relevant to many questions in behavioral ecology," Mahadevan said. "Our study suggests strategies that might well be much broader than the instantiation we have focused on.".

According to recent reports, liu noted that she has long been interested in designing safer and more efficient crowded spaces. This research points toward a future where the movement of large groups, whether robots, vehicles, or people, could be predicted and optimized using mathematical tools.

The results suggest that introducing controlled variability into movement patterns may improve flow in many real-world systems, from factory floors to city streets.

Industry observers note that funding for the research came from the National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program under Grant No. DGE 2140743, along with grants from the Simons Foundation and the Henri Seydoux Fund.

Quantum AI just got shockingly good at predicting chaos

📅 18 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (950 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A newly introduced study led by researchers at UCL (University College London) demonstrates that combining quantum computing with artificial intelligence can significantly improve predictions of complex physical systems over long periods.
  • The results, published in Science Advances, could enhance simulations of how liquids and gases behave, known as fluid dynamics.
  • Recent findings suggest that the improved accuracy appears to come from how quantum computers process information.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A newly introduced study led by researchers at UCL (University College London) demonstrates that combining quantum computing with artificial intelligence can significantly improve predictions of complex physical systems over long periods. The hybrid approach outperforms leading models that rely only on conventional computers.

The results, published in Science Advances, could enhance simulations of how liquids and gases behave, known as fluid dynamics. These types of models are essential in fields such as climate science, transportation, medicine, and energy production.

Why Quantum Computing Makes a Difference.

Recent findings suggest that the improved accuracy appears to come from how quantum computers process information. Unlike traditional computers that use bits set to either 1 or 0, quantum computers use qubits, which can exist as 1, 0, or anything in between. In addition, each qubit can influence others, allowing a relatively small number of qubits to represent an enormous number of possible states.

Professor Peter Coveney, senior author from UCL Chemistry and the Advanced Research Computing Centre, explained the challenge: "To make predictions about complex systems, we can either run a full simulation, which might take weeks -- often too long to be useful -- or we can use an AI model which is quicker but more unreliable over longer time scales.

"Our quantum-informed AI model means we could provide more accurate predictions quickly. Making predictions about fluid flow and turbulence is a fundamental science challenge but it also has many applications. Our method can be used in climate forecasting, in modeling blood flow and the interaction of molecules, or to better design wind farms so they generate more energy.".

How the Hybrid Quantum-AI Method Works.

Recent findings suggest that although quantum computers are widely expected to surpass classical machines in power, their real-world use has so far been limited. This new approach integrates quantum computing into a specific stage of the AI training process.

Typically, AI models learn from large datasets generated by simulations or observations. In this case, the data is first processed by a quantum computer, which identifies key statistical patterns that remain stable over time. These patterns, known as invariant statistical properties, are then used to guide the training of an AI model running on a conventional supercomputer.

Higher Accuracy With Less Memory.

Industry observers note that the quantum-informed AI system delivered about 20 percent greater accuracy compared to standard AI models that did not use quantum-derived patterns. It also maintained stable predictions over longer periods, even when modeling chaotic systems.

Another major advantage was efficiency. The method required hundreds of times less memory, making it far more practical for large-scale simulations.

Quantum Effects Behind the Efficiency.

This performance boost comes from two defining features of quantum computing. Entanglement allows qubits to influence each other regardless of distance, while superposition enables a qubit to exist in multiple states at once until measured. Together, these properties allow quantum systems to process vast amounts of information in a compact form.

Demonstrating Practical Quantum Advantage.

First author Maida Wang of the UCL Centre for Computational Science said: "Our fresh method appears to demonstrate 'quantum advantage' in a practical way -- that is, the quantum computer outperforms what is possible through classical computing alone. These findings could inspire the development of novel classical approaches that achieve even higher accuracy, though they would likely lack the remarkable data compression and parameter efficiency offered by our method. The next steps are to scale up the method using larger datasets and to apply it to real-world situations which typically involve even more complexity. In addition, a provable theoretical framework will be proposed.".

According to recent reports, co-first author Xiao Xue, from Advanced Research Computing at UCL, added: "In this work, we demonstrate for the first time that quantum computing can be meaningfully integrated with classical machine learning methods to tackle complex dynamical systems, including fluid mechanics. It is exciting to see this kind of 'quantum-informed' approach moving towards practical use.".

Capturing the Physics of Complex Systems.

The researchers suggest that quantum computers are particularly well suited to modeling these systems because they can compactly represent their underlying physics. Many complex systems behave in ways that resemble quantum effects, where changes in one region can influence distant parts of the system, similar to entanglement.

Overcoming Limits of Current Quantum Hardware.

According to recent reports, current quantum computers face challenges such as noise, errors, and interference, which often require large numbers of measurements. The latest method avoids these issues by using the quantum computer only once during the workflow, rather than repeatedly exchanging data between quantum and classical systems.

Experiment Details and Future Potential.

The study used a 20-qubit IQM quantum computer connected to powerful classical computing resources at the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre in Germany.

To function, quantum computers must operate at extremely low temperatures, around minus 273C (close to absolute zero, colder than anything in space).

The research was funded by UCL and the UK's Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), with additional support from IQM Quantum Computers and the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre in Munich.

As researchers continue to scale up this approach, it could open the door to more accurate and efficient predictions across a wide range of scientific and engineering applications.

Latest Update: Birdwatching expert gives final verdict on GTA 6’s birds after finding every single one

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that when you think of GTA 6, taking relaxing cross-country trips in search of local flora and fauna probably isn’t the first thing that comes to mind.
